title: 4 cybersecurity steps every organization should take in the age of AI
summary: AI is transforming cybersecurity, but the fundamentals remain essential. Learn why addressing tech debt, strengthening visibility, securing AI agents, and defending at machine speed are critical to building trust in the AI era.
body_markdown:
## The case for a stronger defense


This summer gave us a preview of the next era of cyber conflict. Frontier AI models under evaluation slipped their controls and broke into external systems they were never authorized to access. More concerning, in many cases, developers discovered these incidents only weeks or even months later. Breakthrough AI was only part of the story. Each incident exploited the oldest weaknesses in computing: too much access, too little visibility, and patches that arrived too late. Old failures at machine speed. AI doesn’t replace the fundamentals. It raises the price of neglecting them.


Adversaries are already using off-the-shelf AI technologies to exploit the same gaps. And they are weaponizing AI to do it at speed, scale, and sophistication


. A few weeks ago, Microsoft revealed that Storm-0940, a China-aligned hacking group,


[used an AI framework to attack hundreds of organizations at once](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/10/21/storm-0940-uses-artex-agentic-ai-connectwise-supply-chain-compromise/) , in some cases obtaining privileged cloud access in under three hours. Attackers are now using AI to find software flaws and identity and networking secrets faster than the world can fix them.


### Why leaders should care


Frontier AI capabilities will diffuse. As they do, the advantage will depend on who can deploy them securely and use them most effectively. The transition, which we are living through, has the potential to be the most challenging and dangerous: offensive capabilities can diffuse faster than organizations can address decades of tech debt. In order to be in the race, organizations must first get the basics right. It is telling that some of the most recent cybersecurity incidents, such as the hacking of supermarket refrigerators in Europe, do not involve AI


. Addressing this tech debt is the starting point for enabling trusted tech.


Ultimately, the winners of the AI race will diffuse AI into all of their operations, including adopting AI to increase safety and the security of their organization. Intelligence can’t scale without trust. Securing AI is no longer a technical issue for the IT department; it is a governance responsibility that sits with the board. In the future, boards must understand how many AI agents are in the organization


, what resources they can access, what actions they can take independently, and how the organization is monitoring and managing them. People will only use the technology they trust.


### Four moves that would make a difference today in any organization


1. **Address tech debt:** Change default passwords and retire software and hardware that no one patches or secures.
2. **Close the patching gap:** A patch can also reveal the flaw it closes, and AI can dramatically accelerate the path from disclosure to exploitation in minutes. Measure time to fix, not flaws found.
3. **Radical observability:** Learn from the incidents. Treat AI testing as part of the security perimeter and treat agents as[insider risks.](https://snscratchpad.com/posts/models-as-insider-risks/) Establish[common, open approaches](https://news.microsoft.com/source/2026/11/17/microsoft-and-organizations-across-industries-launch-ai-transparency-initiative-to-strengthen-enterprise-trust-in-ai-models-and-agents/) so you can see, verify, and control AI.
4. **Defend at machine speed:** Put AI to work for defense, with people keeping authority over consequential decisions.


### The boring truth about AI security


No single breakthrough will secure the AI era. The unglamorous basics will: strong identity, least privilege, full visibility, and fast, verified patching


, applied with new speed and discipline. Done well, security stops being a brake on AI and becomes the reason to adopt it with confidence.


The window is open, but not for long. Adversaries already use AI at scale. We must quickly address tech debt so we can more effectively leverage AI for cybersecurity and positive societal innovation. Those who move now can turn a temporary lead into a lasting advantage. The frontier will belong to those who secure it—address tech debt,


close the patching gap, treat AI agents as insider risks, and defend at machine speed.


Read more in Microsoft’s


[white paper](https://aka.ms/SecurityFundamentals) about how AI is helping defenders and how we can collectively secure the fundamentals and ensure we capture the benefits of AI.


To learn more about technologies that defend at machine speed, including[Microsoft Agent 365](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-agent-365) for managing AI agents and[Microsoft Perception](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/11/17/security-for-the-agentic-era-powered-by-microsoft-perception/) for defending with AI at scale, visit the


[Microsoft Security Blog.](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/)
